title: SWAP 4.3.1 H_ENPR modified-MvG source reconciliation and relation to near-saturation closure research

parameter_semantics.KSATFIT: SWAP source describes this as saturated hydraulic conductivity fitted on the VG relation from laboratory data.
parameter_semantics.KSATEXM: SWAP source describes this as saturated hydraulic conductivity examined/measured in laboratory or field.
parameter_semantics.H_ENPR: SWAP source describes this as soil-water entry pressure head for the modified Mualem-Van Genuchten curve.
parameter_semantics.LEXP: Mualem pore-connectivity exponent used by the conductivity relation.

h_enpr_retention_semantics.active_condition: H_ENPR<=-0.01 cm for the default MvG route
h_enpr_retention_semantics.wet_join_branch: For h>=1.05*H_ENPR and h<0, SWAP uses a source-derived rational continuation theta=theta_s+term_105_ab*h/(1+term_105_a*h) that joins the normalized branch and reaches theta_s at h=0.
h_enpr_retention_semantics.saturated_branch: For h>=0, theta=theta_s unless elasticity is explicitly active.

h_enpr_matrix_conductivity_semantics.dry_matrix_branch: For h<H_ENPR, se=f(h)/s_enpr and K_m=KSATFIT*se^LEXP*((1-F(f(h)))/(1-F(s_enpr)))^2, with F(x)=(1-x^(1/m))^m.
h_enpr_matrix_conductivity_semantics.normalization_property: The dry branch reaches exactly KSATFIT at H_ENPR, so H_ENPR defines a finite-air-entry normalized matrix-conductivity relation.
h_enpr_matrix_conductivity_semantics.upper_cap: The source caps the non-KSATEXM result at KSATFIT.

common_structure: normalized Mualem matrix conductivity that reaches a fitted matching conductivity at the air-entry state
distinction between a fitted matrix conductivity scale and a measured saturated conductivity is available in SWAP through KSATFIT and KSATEXM
relation_to_schaap_van_genuchten_2006.important_difference: SWAP H_ENPR retention uses a rational near-entry continuation toward theta_s instead of the exact published MMVG flat theta_s plateau above h_s. SWAP H_ENPR therefore must not be called the published 2006 MMVG model without qualification.
relation_to_schaap_van_genuchten_2006.published_bridge_relevance: Schaap and van Genuchten 2006 provides a literature-backed pressure-dependent log-conductivity bridge from matrix K_m toward measured K_s. This is a plausible separate physical closure to combine with the existing SWAP H_ENPR matrix semantics, but such a hybrid is a new SWAP5 hydraulic closure, not legacy KSATEXM and not verbatim published MMVG.

legacy_composition_finding.finding: Legacy active KSATEXM takes precedence over H_ENPR K_m but uses relsatthr and ksatthr derived from unmodified VG at h=-2 cm. With H_ENPR active this creates a shifted activation head and a discontinuous downward K jump.
legacy_composition_finding.canonical_consequence: Do not expose H_ENPR<0 plus the legacy KSATEXM extension as an ordinary canonical SWAP5 composition.

architecture_consequences: Near-saturation conductivity closure identity belongs to physical configuration, not solver policy.
FullRichards and RossFast must consume the same closure object and immutable derived parameters.
A requested legacy exact-KSATEXM law must not be silently replaced by an H_ENPR/SvG-style bridge for performance reasons.
Explicit SWAP macropore physics must remain separate; any conductivity bridge motivated partly by macro/mesopore effects needs a double-counting analysis before combination.
Derived near-saturation coefficients and Ross face tables are immutable parameter payloads, not persistent column state.

recommended_candidate_lineage.rationale: Uses existing SWAP finite-air-entry physics and source parameter meanings while replacing the incompatible legacy -2 cm linear-in-S extension by an explicit literature-backed continuous pressure-dependent bridge.
